title: Caching and revalidation
description: Understand Next.js caching layers, cache tags, and how to revalidate content when underlying data changes.

data.text: Next.js caches at multiple levels. The **Data Cache** stores the result of `fetch` calls and database queries. The **Full Route Cache** keeps rendered HTML for repeat visitors. The **Client Router Cache** preserves page state during in-app navigation. Each layer can be configured independently.

Revalidation is how you tell the cache that a piece of content is no longer fresh. You can revalidate by **time** (every 60 seconds), **tag** (when a specific event happens), or **on-demand** (after a mutation). Picking the right strategy depends on how stale the data can safely be.

data.title: Cache tags
data.text: Tags let you group related cached content. When a post is updated, revalidate the `posts` tag, and every page or fetch that used that tag refreshes automatically.

data.title: Cache with tags and on-demand revalidation
data.content: Tag a fetch and revalidate after a mutation.

data.title: Force dynamic for personalized data
data.content: Skip the cache when data must be fresh per request.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Data Cache, Full Route Cache, and Client Router Cache serve different purposes.
Use time-based revalidation for content that changes predictably.
Use cache tags for fine-grained invalidation after mutations.
data.takeaway: Think of caching as a spectrum. Cache aggressively, but know how to invalidate precisely when data changes.
